sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct used for surface characterization; surface expression confirmed (construct described as enabling surface detection). Electrophysiological function of the HA-tagged construct relative to untagged KCNE5 is not explicitly reported in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly states the HA tag was placed at the extracellular N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored KCNE5. The canonical topology assigns residues 1–59 as extracellular with no signal peptide, leaving exactly one extracellular N-terminal junction: the prepend before residue 1 (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M). Python confirmed residue 1 = M and that the TM boundary begins 59 residues downstream (residue 60), well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. No specific residue number is cited in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Full-length, membrane-anchored HA-KCNE5 construct generated by site-directed mutagenesis (QuikChange); HA epitope introduced into the extracellular N-terminus for surface characterization. No signal peptide is present in the canonical topology (residues 1–59 are entirely extracellular), so the N-terminal prepend (before residue 1) is the sole extracellular N-terminal junction.

sources.claim: HA-Kv6.4 and HA-KCNE5 constructs were generated by introducing the HA epitope (YPYDVPDYA) into the extracellular S1-S2 loop and the extracellular N-terminus, respectively, by PCR amplification using the QuikChange TM Site-Directed Mutagenesis kit (Stratagene, La Jolla, CA, USA) and mutant primers.

literature_notes: L2 (KCNE5-YFP, C-terminal fusion) was evaluated but the C-terminus falls entirely within the intracellular domain (residues 81–142 per the authoritative topology landmarks); it is recorded in other_positions as an intracellular tag. Only one extracellular surface site is supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal YFP fusion (KCNE5-YFP via peYFP-N1 vector); residue 142 (V) lies in the intracellular domain (residues 81–142), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-accessible site.
